title: Broadcasting Services Amendment (Advertising for Sports Betting) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would restrict sports betting promotions on commercial television and radio and subscription television by adding conditions to broadcasters' licences.
It would ban advertisements containing numerical betting odds at any time and require other sports betting advertisements to be broadcast after 9pm.
The restrictions would also cover odds information near sports programs and paid promotion within editorial content, applying from the day of Royal Assent.
changes: Odds information would be prohibited within a 30-minute window of sports events and sports-related programs.
Commentators and guests could not discuss betting services outside scheduled advertising breaks where the broadcaster received payment.
Commercial radio and subscription television licensees would face the same restrictions as commercial television licensees.
summary.affected: Commercial television and radio licensees, subscription television licensees, paid commentators and guests are affected.
